knowledge_point.title: Solving a Challenging System of Linear Equations Using Substitution

question.:question/problem:
Given the system of equations below, what is the value of $y-x?$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}21x-9y=0 \\ 5y-15x+10=0\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We number the equations so that we can refer to them more easily:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}21x-9y=0 & \,\,(1) \\ 5y-15x+10=0 & \,\,(2)\end{aligned}
$$

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $(2),$ we can isolate $y$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5y-15x+10 & =0 \\ 5y & =15x-10 \\ y & =3x-2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $3x-2$  into equation $(1)$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}21x-9y & =0 \\ 21x-9(3x-2) & =0 \\ 21x-27x+18 & =0 \\ -6x+18 & =0 \\ 18 & =6x \\ 3 & =x\end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute $x=3$ into $y=3x-2,$ then we can find the value of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =3x-2 \\ y & =3(3)-2 \\ y & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=3,\,y=7.$ So,

$$
y-x=7-3=4.
$$
